scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

F-01.statement: CRM dispute tickets (2440) have median response time 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA.

F-02.statement: Field route-log data shows 88% route completion against a 95% target for manual-read accounts (9200 accounts) over Aug-Sep 2026.

F-03.statement: Billing-db tariff_change_log shows 0 records, i.e. no tariff rate changes in the queried period.

F-04.statement: Billing-db disputed_bills_by_read_type shows 1240 disputed bills with ESTIMATED reads and 1785 with ACTUAL reads.

F-05.statement: CRM dispute_volume_monthly shows 610 disputes in 2026-06, 590 in 2026-07, 1180 in 2026-08, and 1260 in 2026-09.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 permits the utility to request route priority changes but requires execution only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-TICKET-RESPONSE-SPEED.statement: The August-September dispute surge is primarily a ticket-handling/response problem (slow or inconsistent answers), fixable by an AI agent that auto-answers tickets.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August introduced systematic bill errors, causing the dispute surge.

H-AMI-DATA-QUALITY.statement: Degraded AMI read delivery or validation via MDMS (vendor-run) caused increased estimate substitution and inaccurate bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: Deteriorating manual meter-read collection or upload by the contracted field service (MeterWorks) led to more missed/estimated reads and billing errors.

H-SEASONAL-USAGE.statement: Bills are substantively correct and the dispute surge reflects genuine seasonal consumption increases that customers find surprising, not a process defect.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECTION-R.statement: A billing import validation rule rejects AMI reads flagged as high consumption (billing_import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution and driving most of the ESTIMATED-read dispute population.

interpretation_history.interpretation: CRM data (2440 tickets) shows median response time 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days, both inside the 3.0-day SLA, indicating ticket-handling speed is not currently a measurable gap in how disputes are being answered.

Route-log data (E-02) shows manual-read route completion of 88% against a 95% target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts, during the Aug-Sep 2026 period that matches the dispute surge window — a measurable shortfall in field meter-read collection, not yet linked to disputes directly.

Billing-db's tariff change log returned zero records, indicating no tariff rate changes occurred in the relevant period — ruling out a tariff-rate change as a cause of incorrect bills, independent of the billing import validation rule question.

Of disputed bills broken down by meter-read type, 1785 involved an ACTUAL read and 1240 involved an ESTIMATED read, meaning actual-read bills account for the majority (about 59%) of disputes, not estimated/substituted reads.

E-04 still shows disputed bills split 1785 ACTUAL vs 1240 ESTIMATED by read type (billing-db). It no longer supports a clean ACTUAL-vs-ESTIMATED mechanism split or a billing defect exclusive to ACTUAL reads, since E-12 shows the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes are themselves caused by billing-import rejection (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION of valid AMI reads), not field/AMI delivery failure.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states there has been no tariff change this year; this stakeholder claim is consistent with E-03's authoritative tariff_change_log showing zero records, reinforcing (but not independently proving, since it is a non-authoritative claim) that a tariff-rate change is not the cause of incorrect bills.

CRM's monthly dispute volume data shows 610 and 590 disputes in June and July, then 1180 and 1260 in August and September — confirming the surge in raw ticket volume began in August and roughly doubled, matching the timing framing in CL-01, but this count alone says nothing about why disputes rose.

E-06 still shows dispute volume rising from 610/590 (Jun/Jul) to 1180/1260 (Aug/Sep), confirming the surge's timing and rough doubling. It no longer supports the premise that this timing reflects a billing defect specific to ACTUAL-read bills, since E-12 shows the ESTIMATED-read population is also driven by a billing-import rejection mechanism, undermining the ACTUAL-vs-ESTIMATED causal split the timing was used to anchor.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims field reading has been short three readers since July, causing routes to run late and those customers to get estimated bills. This is a non-authoritative stakeholder claim offering a causal mechanism (staffing shortage) for the route shortfall already measured in E-02, but it comes from a stakeholder incentivized to secure headcount increase and flagged as biased toward staffing attribution.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract document confirms that the utility may request route priority changes but such changes are only executed after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD), consistent with the already-recorded K-DISPATCH constraint; it is a procedural/authority document, not evidence about the billing dispute cause.

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-09 shows 320 distinct accounts received estimated bills last cycle, spread across 40 distinct routes, with no causal or dispute linkage yet established in the record itself. Compared against E-04's 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes, this single-cycle estimated-account count is notably smaller, suggesting the field route completion shortfall (E-02) accounts for only part of the estimated-read dispute population.

E-10.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes (E-10) returns 14 routes with distinct completion values (sample: route R-00 at 0.70 completion), giving a per-route breakdown of the manual-read completion shortfall already measured in aggregate by E-02 (88% vs 95% target). It identifies which/how many routes are lagging but does not itself quantify how many accounts or disputes trace to these specific routes.

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (non-authoritative, message) reports vendor ticket TX-4471 shows MDMS export access for Lakeside now provisioned; this is a stakeholder claim about access status, not a confirmed tool-level verification, and does not itself speak to bill-error causation.

E-12 (MDMS, now access-provisioned) breaks the AMI-channel read events behind disputed estimated-read accounts into two groups: 1184 where an AMI read arrived before cutoff but billing import rejected it as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (exported_to_billing=true), and 56 where no AMI read was received at all (NO_READ_RECEIVED, exported_to_billing=false). This points to a billing-import validation rejection, not AMI/vendor read-delivery failure, as the dominant mechanism behind most of these estimated-read disputes; the 1184+56=1240 total also matches E-04's full ESTIMATED dispute count, suggesting this population may be entirely AMI-metered rather than manual-read.

U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.question: Does the billing-config rule change log (DA-RULES) show an actual validation-rule change coinciding with August that explains incorrect ACTUAL-read bills?
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.decision_impact: Confirms or refutes H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE as the dominant mechanism; if absent, the root cause must be re-investigated before any remediation claim is made.
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.resolution_path: Query billing-config change log for entries in Jul-Sep 2026 and cross-reference timestamps with the August dispute surge onset (E-06).
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.safe_placeholder: Treat H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE as unconfirmed; limit scope to diagnostic investigation (investigate_billing_rule_change) and withhold any remediation claim until the log is checked.

U-AMI-DATA-ACCESS.question: Will MDMS vendor access be provisioned (currently ACCESS_PENDING), and does AMI read-event data reveal any contributing issue for the ESTIMATED-read subset (1240) of disputes?
U-AMI-DATA-ACCESS.decision_impact: Determines whether AMI/MDMS issues contribute to the smaller ESTIMATED-read dispute subset; tool mdms-export is currently DEGRADED (ACCESS_PENDING) with no fallback, so this path may stay unresolved within the contest window.
U-AMI-DATA-ACCESS.resolution_path: Continue pending vendor provisioning of MDMS export access (mdms-export, DEGRADED/ACCESS_PENDING); once granted, verify H-MDMS-BILL handoff delivery/semantic validity before relying on this data.
U-AMI-DATA-ACCESS.safe_placeholder: Proceed on the dominant ACTUAL-read mechanism (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE) without AMI data; treat the ESTIMATED-read subset as a known limitation pending vendor access.
U-AMI-DATA-ACCESS.resolution: MDMS access is now functioning; E-12 shows for the ESTIMATED-read dispute subset 1184/1240 AMI read events were valid reads rejected at billing import (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) and only 56 were true no-read-received cases, i.e. a billing-import defect, not AMI delivery/validation degradation.

U-ROUTE-COMPLETION-CONTRIBUTIO.question: Does the field route completion shortfall (88% vs 95%, E-02) materially contribute to the ESTIMATED-read portion of disputes (1240), separately from the dominant billing-rule mechanism?
U-ROUTE-COMPLETION-CONTRIBUTIO.decision_impact: If route completion drives part of the ESTIMATED-read disputes, remediation may need a dispatch route-priority change (push_route_update) in addition to the billing-rule fix.
U-ROUTE-COMPLETION-CONTRIBUTIO.resolution_path: Cross-reference route-log completion-shortfall accounts (E-02) against ESTIMATED-read disputed-bill accounts (E-04); also verify H-FIELD-BILL handoff delivery/semantic validity (manual reads, ORG-FIELD to ORG-UTIL).
U-ROUTE-COMPLETION-CONTRIBUTIO.safe_placeholder: Treat route completion as a secondary, unconfirmed contributor (A-FIELD-ROUTE-SECONDARY); any push_route_update stays subject to K-DISPATCH confirmation by SH-FIELD and is not executed on this unknown alone.
U-ROUTE-COMPLETION-CONTRIBUTIO.resolution: E-12's AMI-channel counts (1184+56=1240) exactly match E-04's full ESTIMATED dispute count, tentatively indicating this dispute population is AMI-metered rather than manual-read, so the manual-read route completion shortfall (E-02) may not directly drive it; account/channel overlap confirmation still needed.

U-TICKET-VOLUME-AS-PROXY.question: Is dispute ticket volume alone a valid proxy for 'problem fixed', given a likely lag between a billing-rule fix and the next billing cycle's tickets dropping?
U-TICKET-VOLUME-AS-PROXY.decision_impact: Affects how dispute-volume recovery is validated; using raw monthly ticket count without a lag window could prematurely declare success or failure.
U-TICKET-VOLUME-AS-PROXY.resolution_path: Compare dispute-volume recovery against billing-cycle length and the DA-RULES fix-confirmation date; require at least one full post-fix billing cycle before measuring recovery.
U-TICKET-VOLUME-AS-PROXY.safe_placeholder: Report the dispute_volume trend alongside the rule-change confirmation date rather than declaring recovery before one post-fix billing cycle has elapsed.

A-RULE-CHANGE-CAUSAL-LINK.statement: The dispute surge stems from a billing import/validation rule change around August, inferred from E-04's actual-read dominance pattern; no billing-config rule-change log entry has yet been directly cited to confirm this.

A-FIELD-ROUTE-SECONDARY.statement: The field route completion shortfall (E-02) and staffing claim (E-07, CL-03) are a secondary contributor to disputes, not the dominant one, because E-04 shows disputes concentrated in ACTUAL (not ESTIMATED) reads.

A-BASELINE-VALIDITY.statement: The pre-August baseline (~600 disputes/month, from June and July figures) is a valid comparison point for measuring recovery, absent other seasonal confounds.
